subject.title: fix: surface cron errors for empty isolated agent replies

question: Should delivery-requested cron isolated-agent runs with no final payload fail closed as cron errors by default when they were not explicitly silent and were not already delivered by a verified message-tool path?
rationale: The PR fixes a dark-lane failure but changes terminal status and delivery accounting for existing empty-completion cron runs, which is a compatibility-sensitive behavior choice.

options.title: Accept Fail-Closed Cron Error
options.body: Proceed after concrete redacted proof shows the empty-payload lane records an error and maintainers accept the default status-semantics change.

options.title: Require A Compatibility Gate
options.body: Ask for a default-compatible policy or explicit opt-in before turning all unmarked delivery-requested empty completions into errors.

options.title: Defer To Parser-Only Repair
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want upstream parser fixes to land first before adding the cron-level safety net.

recommendation.title: Accept Fail-Closed Cron Error
recommendation.body: Proceed after concrete redacted proof shows the empty-payload lane records an error and maintainers accept the default status-semantics change.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans cron terminal-state semantics and the isolated cron runner boundary that Peter Steinberger has substantial history shaping.
